summary:
Fifth candidate (action=obligation) on a client-contract gap, plus a map extension; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Sourced discrepancy: the library wires a shutdown escape into some futures (restoreFuture in restoreUserSnapshot and installSnapshot, configurationsFuture in takeSnapshot) but not into the logFuture created by Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier (api.go:826-852), while deferError.Error returns ErrRaftShutdown only through that field (future.go:92-120) and Shutdown closes the node without draining the apply channel (api.go:1012-1030). With the documented BatchApplyCh option the apply channel is buffered, so a request can be accepted and then dropped by shutdown with neither a response nor an escape. A local construction run confirmed it: after Shutdown, responded_after_shutdown was false and shutdown_escape was false. The consequence is a permanently blocked caller — a client-contract hang, not a consensus-safety violation.

Product contents: obligation claim-client-future-shutdown-escape (implementation_semantics) — every client-facing future the library returns can complete, either by a raft loop responding it or by carrying the node's shutdown channel so Error() returns ErrRaftShutdown; one question grounded on the new principal Fact f-client-completion-escape (A7), direct Behavior b-client-future (A7), lifecycle establishment, with supporting behaviors b-leader-loop-commit-consume and b-commit-index-advance for the A1 completion lifecycle; and one physical binding (symbol ApplyLog over api.go:826-852).

Map extension (base version 17): the shutdown branch added to b-client-future (which now also produces the new Fact), the new Fact, and two sources; no accepted object's meaning, identity or edges changed, so the four confirmed findings and all accepted results keep their basis.

Retained counterevidence and unknowns, not suppressed: Shutdown is usually process end, so a blocked caller may not matter; the default BatchApplyCh=false makes the channel unbuffered and narrows the window; and the Apply docs promise an enqueue timeout rather than completion. Whether VerifyLeader's verifyFuture, configurationChangeFuture and userSnapshotFuture share the gap, and whether the maintainers intend the asymmetry, are explicit premises for the check that follows.
